def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p

                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:

                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p

    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]

from functools import lru_cache


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def _possible_nonfixed_counts():
    """Bitsets of attainable nonfixed counts for every pair of budgets."""
    limit = 30
    possible = [[1] * (limit + 1) for _ in range(limit + 1)]
    for rows in range(1, limit + 1):
        for cols in range(1, limit + 1):
            # Unused vertices become singleton components, hence fixed cells.
            counts = possible[rows - 1][cols] | possible[rows][cols - 1]
            for block_rows in range(2, rows + 1):
                remainder = possible[rows - block_rows]
                for block_cols in range(2, cols + 1):
                    counts |= remainder[cols - block_cols] << (block_rows * block_cols)
            possible[rows][cols] = counts
    return possible


def matrix_with_k_fixed_elements_exists(n: int, k: int) -> bool:
    """ Given an integer n (size of matrix) and k (number of fixed elements),
    determine if there exists an n×n binary matrix with exactly k fixed elements.

    A binary matrix has elements that are either 0 or 1.
    Two matrices A and B are similar if they have the same row sums and column sums.
    An element at position (i,j) in matrix A is fixed if it has the same value
    in all matrices similar to A.

    Args:
        n: Size of the matrix (2 ≤ n ≤ 30)
        k: Number of fixed elements (0 ≤ k ≤ n²)

    Returns:
        True if there exists an n×n binary matrix with exactly k fixed elements,
        False otherwise.

    >>> matrix_with_k_fixed_elements_exists(3, 0)
    True
    >>> matrix_with_k_fixed_elements_exists(3, 9)
    True
    >>> matrix_with_k_fixed_elements_exists(3, 7)
    False
    """
    # Orient each 1 from its row to its column, and each 0 the other way.
    # A cell can change exactly when its edge lies on a directed (alternating)
    # cycle, equivalently when its endpoints share a strongly connected component.
    # Every nontrivial component uses r >= 2 rows and c >= 2 columns and
    # contributes exactly r*c nonfixed cells. Different components use disjoint
    # rows and columns.
    # Conversely, every K_{r,c}, r,c >= 2, has a strongly connected orientation:
    # start with a directed four-cycle and duplicate row/column vertices.
    # Order any such blocks and singleton vertices, directing all cross-block
    # edges forward. Thus every collection counted by the DP is realizable.
    if not 2 <= n <= 30 or not 0 <= k <= n * n:
        return False
    nonfixed = n * n - k
    return bool((_possible_nonfixed_counts()[n][n] >> nonfixed) & 1)

def count_event_ways(n: int, x: int, y: int) -> int:
    """ Calculate the number of ways an event can take place.
    
    An event is being held for n performers. When a performer arrives, they are assigned 
    to one of the x stages. All performers assigned to the same stage will perform together 
    as a band, though some stages might remain empty.
    
    After all performances are completed, the jury will award each band a score in the 
    range [1, y].
    
    Two events are considered different if either:
    - Any performer is assigned a different stage
    - Any band is awarded a different score
    
    Args:
        n: Number of performers (1 <= n <= 1000)
        x: Number of stages (1 <= x <= 1000)
        y: Maximum score that can be awarded (1 <= y <= 1000)
    
    Returns:
        The total number of possible ways the event can take place, modulo 10^9 + 7
    
    >>> count_event_ways(1, 2, 3)
    6
    >>> count_event_ways(5, 2, 1)
    32
    >>> count_event_ways(3, 3, 4)
    684
    """
    mod = 10**9 + 7
    limit = min(n, x)
    # dp[k] counts assignments and scores with exactly k occupied stages.
    dp = [0] * (limit + 1)
    dp[0] = 1
    for performers in range(1, n + 1):
        for occupied in range(min(performers, limit), 0, -1):
            # Join one of the occupied bands, or open and score a new band.
            dp[occupied] = (
                occupied * dp[occupied]
                + (x - occupied + 1) * y * dp[occupied - 1]
            ) % mod
        dp[0] = 0
    return sum(dp) % mod

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

    def sums(x, start):
        k = size-x if x <= root else N//x-1
        total = M*(prime_count[k]-start)
        bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
        i = start
        while i < plen and squares[i] <= x:
            p = primes[i]
            bw = bad_weights[p % 3]
            power = p
            e = 1

from math import isqrt

    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.

        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],

    plen = len(primes)

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

        bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
        i = start
        while i < plen and squares[i] <= x:
            p = primes[i]
            bw = bad_weights[p % 3]
            power = p
            e = 1

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0

from math import isqrt


def count_square_permutations(n: int, s: str) -> int:
    """Count distinct squares represented by permutations of all digits of s.

    Leading zeros are allowed. In particular, '010' represents both the
    squares 1 (as '001') and 100, so its answer is 2.
    """
    digits = sorted(s)
    smallest = int(''.join(digits))
    largest = int(''.join(reversed(digits)))
    lower = isqrt(smallest)
    if lower * lower < smallest:
        lower += 1
    upper = isqrt(largest)

    # Decimal digit sums are invariant modulo nine. Only these root
    # residues can produce squares with the required digit sum.
    residue = sum(ord(digit) - ord('0') for digit in s) % 9
    root_residues = [r for r in range(9) if r * r % 9 == residue]
    answer = 0
    for root_residue in root_residues:
        start = lower + (root_residue - lower) % 9
        for root in range(start, upper + 1, 9):
            # Padding gives every integer its unique length-n decimal
            # representation, including any required leading zeros.
            if sorted(str(root * root).zfill(n)) == digits:
                answer += 1
    return answer

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))

def count_polish_sequences(n: int, a: list[int]) -> int:
    """Count Polish sequences of length n lexicographically <= a, modulo 998244353.

    A Polish sequence is the preorder list of child counts of an ordered
    rooted tree. The sequence (0) represents a leaf.

    Args:
        n: The sequence length, with 1 <= n <= 300000.
        a: The upper bound of length n, with 0 <= a[i] < n.

    Returns:
        The number of Polish sequences lexicographically at most a.
    """
    mod = 998244353
    limit = 2 * n
    factorial = [1] * (limit + 1)
    for i in range(1, limit + 1):
        factorial[i] = factorial[i - 1] * i % mod
    inverse_factorial = [1] * (limit + 1)
    inverse_factorial[limit] = pow(factorial[limit], mod - 2, mod)
    for i in range(limit, 0, -1):
        inverse_factorial[i - 1] = inverse_factorial[i] * i % mod

    def choose(total: int, selected: int) -> int:
        if selected < 0 or selected > total:
            return 0
        return (factorial[total] * inverse_factorial[selected] % mod
                * inverse_factorial[total - selected] % mod)

    answer = 0
    pending = 1
    for i, value in enumerate(a):
        remaining = n - i - 1
        # Count the first smaller entry, then fill the remaining open slots.
        # A forest with q roots and m vertices has
        # C(2m-q-1, m-1) - C(2m-q-1, m) possible preorder lists.
        # Summing over the smaller entries telescopes by the hockey-stick
        # identity into four binomial coefficients.
        low = pending - 1
        high = min(pending + value - 2, remaining)
        if remaining == 0:
            if pending == 1 and value > 0:
                answer += 1
        elif low <= high:
            upper = 2 * remaining - low
            lower = 2 * remaining - high - 1
            answer += (choose(upper, remaining)
                       - choose(lower, remaining)
                       - choose(upper, remaining + 1)
                       + choose(lower, remaining + 1))
            answer %= mod

        pending += value - 1
        # The equal prefix must leave between one and remaining open slots,
        # except that the complete sequence must leave exactly zero.
        if pending == 0 or pending > remaining:
            if remaining == 0 and pending == 0:
                answer += 1
            break

    return answer % mod

text: Inspected current lcbhard_16 main; current-main suite pending to distinguish stale timeout reports. Concrete optimization: in sums(x,start), tail primes with p^2<=x<p^3 have only e=1 and a prime cofactor. Each total term is M^2*(pi(x//p)-i-1)+coeff[2]. Bad term: p≡2 mod3 -> coeff[2]; p≡1 -> M^2*(bad_pi(x//p)-bad_prefix[i+1]); p=3 -> same bad prime-count term +coeff[2]. Thus batch this entire tail via NumPy quotient/index lookup and residue masks, converting summed counts to Python int before multiplying M^2 to avoid int64 overflow. Use a minimum tail length to avoid per-recursion vectorization overhead; small tails can use a simpler direct loop. This removes many inner while/weight/leaf operations while preserving the general recurrence.

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:

                two[:stop] -= a

    else:

        for p in primes:

            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square

    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]

        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:

            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

    def sums(x, start):
        k = size-x if x <= root else N//x-1
        total = M*(prime_count[k]-start)
        bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
        i = start
        while i < plen and squares[i] <= x:
            p = primes[i]
            bw = bad_weights[p % 3]
            power = p
            e = 1

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

    def sums(x, start):

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

    def sums(x, start):
        k = size-x if x <= root else N//x-1
        total = M*(prime_count[k]-start)
        bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
        i = start
        while i < plen and squares[i] <= x:
            p = primes[i]
            bw = bad_weights[p % 3]
            power = p
            e = 1

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

    def sums(x, start):

        bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
        i = start

            p = primes[i]
            bw = bad_weights[p % 3]

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1

def expected_black_ball_position(N: int, K: int) -> int:
    """ There are N-1 white balls and one black ball arranged in a row, with the black ball
    initially at the leftmost position. Takahashi performs K operations, where each operation
    consists of:
    - Choose two integers a and b uniformly at random between 1 and N, inclusive
    - If a ≠ b, swap the a-th and b-th balls from the left
    
    Find the expected position of the black ball after K operations, modulo 998244353.
    
    The result is returned as an integer R where R × Q ≡ P (mod 998244353), where P/Q is
    the expected value expressed as an irreducible fraction.
    
    Args:
        N: Total number of balls (1 ≤ N ≤ 998244352)
        K: Number of operations (1 ≤ K ≤ 10^5)
    
    Returns:
        The expected position modulo 998244353
    
    >>> expected_black_ball_position(2, 1)
    499122178
    >>> expected_black_ball_position(3, 2)
    554580198
    >>> expected_black_ball_position(4, 4)
    592707587
    """
    mod = 998244353
    inverse_n = pow(N, mod - 2, mod)
    # From position x, each other position is reached with probability 2/N^2.
    # Thus E_next = (1 - 2/N) * E + (N + 1)/N.
    equilibrium = (N + 1) * ((mod + 1) // 2) % mod
    decay = pow((1 - 2 * inverse_n) % mod, K, mod)
    return (equilibrium + (1 - equilibrium) * decay) % mod

def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

    def sums(x, start):

        total = M*(prime_count[k]-start)
        bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
        i = start
        while i < plen and squares[i] <= x:
            p = primes[i]
            bw = bad_weights[p % 3]
            power = p
            e = 1

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

    def sums(x, start):
        k = size-x if x <= root else N//x-1
        total = M*(prime_count[k]-start)
        bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
        i = start
        while i < plen and squares[i] <= x:
            p = primes[i]
            bw = bad_weights[p % 3]
            power = p
            e = 1

title: Speed multiplicative summation by aggregating prime-cofactor tail
diff:
--- problems/lcbhard_16/solution.py
+++ problems/lcbhard_16/solution.py
@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
 from math import isqrt
+from bisect import bisect_right
 
 try:
     import numpy as _np
@@ -22,6 +23,7 @@
             sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
     primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
     squares = [p*p for p in primes]
+    cubes = [p*p*p for p in primes]
     values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
     values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
     size = len(values)
@@ -109,7 +111,9 @@
         total = M*(prime_count[k]-start)
         bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
         i = start
-        while i < plen and squares[i] <= x:
+        end = bisect_right(squares, x)
+        complex_end = min(end, bisect_right(cubes, x))
+        while i < complex_end:
             p = primes[i]
             bw = bad_weights[p % 3]
             power = p
@@ -127,6 +131,22 @@
                 power *= p
                 e += 1
             i += 1
+        # If p^3 > x, only the exponent-one term and pure p^2
+        # remain. Sum their unweighted prime counts before multiplying.
+        tail_start = i
+        tail_total = tail_bad = tail_squares = 0
+        for j in range(i, end):
+            p = primes[j]
+            q = x//p
+            k = size-q if q <= root else N//q-1
+            tail_total += prime_count[k]-j-1
+            residue = p % 3
+            if residue != 2:
+                tail_bad += bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[j+1]
+            if residue != 1:
+                tail_squares += 1
+        total += M*M*tail_total+coeff[2]*(end-tail_start)
+        bad += M*M*tail_bad+coeff[2]*tail_squares
         return total % MOD, bad % MOD
 
     total, bad = sums(N, 0)

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one

def min_changes_for_semi_palindromes(s: str, k: int) -> int:
    """ Given a string s and an integer k, partition s into k substrings such that the sum 
    of the number of letter changes required to turn each substring into a semi-palindrome 
    is minimized. Return the minimum number of letter changes required.
    
    A string is a semi-palindrome if:
    - It has length >= 2, AND
    - There exists a positive integer d such that 1 <= d < len and len % d == 0, AND
    - Taking indices that have the same modulo by d forms a palindrome.
    
    For example: "aa", "aba", "adbgad", and "abab" are semi-palindromes.
    "a", "ab", and "abca" are not semi-palindromes.
    
    Args:
        s: A string consisting only of lowercase English letters (2 <= len(s) <= 200)
        k: Number of substrings to partition into (1 <= k <= len(s) / 2)
    
    Returns:
        The minimum number of letter changes required to make all k substrings semi-palindromes.
    
    >>> min_changes_for_semi_palindromes("abcac", 2)
    1
    >>> min_changes_for_semi_palindromes("abcdef", 2)
    2
    >>> min_changes_for_semi_palindromes("aabbaa", 3)
    0
    """
    n = len(s)
    divisors = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for d in range(1, n // 2 + 1):
        for length in range(2 * d, n + 1, d):
            divisors[length].append(d)

    # cost[start][end] uses an exclusive end. For each possible stride,
    # the residue classes are disjoint, so every mismatched mirrored pair
    # requires exactly one independent character change.
    cost = [[n] * (n + 1) for _ in range(n)]
    for length in range(2, n + 1):
        for start in range(n - length + 1):
            best = n
            for d in divisors[length]:
                changes = 0
                for residue in range(d):
                    left = start + residue
                    right = left + length - d
                    while left < right:
                        changes += s[left] != s[right]
                        left += d
                        right -= d
                best = min(best, changes)
                if best == 0:
                    break
            cost[start][start + length] = best

    # After each layer, dp[end] is the optimum for exactly that many
    # substrings covering s[:end]. Every substring has at least two letters.
    dp = [n] * (n + 1)
    dp[0] = 0
    for groups in range(1, k + 1):
        next_dp = [n] * (n + 1)
        for end in range(2 * groups, n + 1):
            next_dp[end] = min(
                dp[start] + cost[start][end]
                for start in range(2 * (groups - 1), end - 1)
            )
        dp = next_dp
    return dp[n]

def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

    def sums(x, start):
        k = size-x if x <= root else N//x-1
        total = M*(prime_count[k]-start)
        bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
        i = start
        while i < plen and squares[i] <= x:
            p = primes[i]
            bw = bad_weights[p % 3]
            power = p
            e = 1

from math import isqrt

try:
    import numpy as _np
except ImportError:
    _np = None

MOD = 998244353


def count_good_sequences(N: int, M: int) -> int:
    """Count length-M positive-integer sequences with product at most N
    whose positive divisors have sum divisible by three, modulo 998244353.
    """
    if N < 2:
        return 0
    root = isqrt(N)
    sieve = bytearray(b"\x01") * (root + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, isqrt(root) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p*p::p] = b"\x00" * ((root-p*p)//p+1)
    primes = [p for p in range(2, root+1) if sieve[p]]
    squares = [p*p for p in primes]
    values = [N//i for i in range(1, root+1)]
    values.extend(range(values[-1]-1, 0, -1))
    size = len(values)

    # Min_25 sieve: remove composites from the two nonzero classes mod 3.
    # Prime 3 is handled separately.  Every floor quotient has index
    # size-v (v <= root), or N//v-1 (v > root).
    one = [(v-1)//3 for v in values]
    two = [(v+1)//3 for v in values]
    before_one = before_two = 0
    bad_prefix = [0]
    for p in primes:
        bad_prefix.append(bad_prefix[-1] + (p % 3 != 2))

    if _np is not None:
        vs = _np.asarray(values, dtype=_np.int64)
        one = _np.asarray(one, dtype=_np.int64)
        two = _np.asarray(two, dtype=_np.int64)
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            q = vs[:stop]//p
            idx = _np.where(q <= root, size-q, N//q-1)
            a = one[idx]-before_one
            b = two[idx]-before_two
            if p % 3 == 1:
                one[:stop] -= a
                two[:stop] -= b
                before_one += 1
            else:
                one[:stop] -= b
                two[:stop] -= a
                before_two += 1
        one = one.tolist()
        two = two.tolist()
    else:
        # The same sieve without an optional numerical dependency.
        for p in primes:
            if p == 3:
                continue
            square = p*p
            stop = size-square+1 if square <= root else N//square
            split = min(stop, N//(p*(root+1)))
            if p % 3 == 1:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                    two[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                before_one += 1
            else:
                for i in range(split):
                    q = values[i]//p
                    j = N//q-1
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                for i in range(split, stop):
                    j = size-values[i]//p
                    one[i] -= two[j]-before_two
                    two[i] -= one[j]-before_one
                before_two += 1

    prime_count = [a+b+(v >= 3) for a,b,v in zip(one,two,values)]
    bad_count = [a+(v >= 3) for a,v in zip(one,values)]
    # A product with prime exponent e has C(M+e-1,e) ordered
    # factorizations. The divisor-sum condition is multiplicative.
    coeff = [1]
    for e in range(1, N.bit_length()+1):
        coeff.append(coeff[-1]*(M+e-1) % MOD * pow(e, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD)
    bad_weights = [
        coeff,
        [c if e % 3 != 2 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
        [c if e % 2 == 0 else 0 for e,c in enumerate(coeff)],
    ]
    plen = len(primes)

    def sums(x, start):
        k = size-x if x <= root else N//x-1

        bad = M*(bad_count[k]-bad_prefix[start])
